description: Hi, We are from Team Red_Stone. We are participating in Dancing with SAR segment.
summary: SAR Tensor is an advanced geodetic decision-support application that transforms complex NASA SAR interferograms (from NISAR and Sentinel-1) into clear, actionable early-warning maps of ground deformation risk.Using NASA’s Earthdata API, the system retrieves Level-2 unwrapped interferograms and applies spatial finite-difference algorithms to compute the full 2D horizontal strain tensor. Unlike traditional line-of-sight displacement maps, SAR Tensor highlights zones of differential shear strain—the true precursors of sinkholes, urban subsidence, and slope failures.A Streamlit + Folium web interface lets municipal engineers and emergency responders instantly switch between real-world case studies (Mexico City, Mekong Delta, Kīlauea), scrub through multi-temporal data, and view a quantitative vulnerability index in real time.By converting inaccessible radar science into an intuitive, open-source tool, SAR Tensor shifts disaster management from reactive cleanup to proactive protection—helping safeguard critical infrastructure and human lives in sinking deltas, expanding cities, and volcanic regions worldwide.
details:
What it does & how it works
SAR Tensor is a cloud-ready geodetic decision-support web application that converts raw NASA SAR interferograms into clear structural-risk maps. The backend programmatically queries NASA’s Earthdata API (Common Metadata Repository + ASF DAAC) to retrieve high-resolution Level-2 unwrapped interferograms from NISAR and Sentinel-1. A custom geodetic engine written in Python (NumPy + SciPy) then computes spatial derivatives of the velocity field to build the complete 2D horizontal strain tensor . From this tensor the system derives maximum shear strain and a quantitative subsurface vulnerability index (0–100).

Users interact with an intuitive Streamlit + Folium frontend that offers three operational modes (Urban Subsidence, Delta Collapse, Volcanic Unrest), a multi-temporal scrubber, and live telemetry panels showing peak LOS velocity, shear strain, dilatation, and risk status.

Benefits

  • Turns mathematically complex, noisy radar data into simple, color-coded risk layers that non-specialists can understand in seconds.
  • Focuses on differential shear strain rather than simple displacement—the actual mechanical driver of sinkholes and structural collapse.
  • Includes intelligent failover to high-resolution simulated grids when live NASA APIs are unavailable, ensuring zero downtime.
  • Fully open-source codebase for transparency and community extension.

Intended impact
Shift disaster management from reactive post-event cleanup to proactive early warning. Municipal engineers, infrastructure operators, and emergency responders can monitor millimeter-scale ground movement months in advance, prioritize inspections, and protect lives and critical assets in rapidly growing cities, coastal deltas, and volcanic zones worldwide.

Tools & technologies

  • Languages: Python
  • Scientific stack: NumPy, SciPy
  • Frontend: Streamlit, Folium / Leaflet
  • Data access: NASA Earthdata API, ASF DAAC
  • Source control & deployment: GitHub, cloud-resilient architecture

Creativity & design factors considered
Our team deliberately moved beyond conventional “pretty displacement maps.” By computing the full strain tensor and highlighting shear concentrations, SAR Tensor reveals hidden failure mechanisms that simple LOS products miss. Design priorities included:

  • Scientific rigor balanced with extreme usability for non-radar experts
  • Real-time interactivity and temporal exploration
  • Reliability under variable network conditions
  • Open-source transparency so any city or research group can adopt and extend the tool
projectRefs: Sentinel-1 Mission (European Space Agency) – data accessed via ASF DAAC / NASA Earthdata
